answer: Timber piles can be copied, but a lineage tax cannot: whenever a key hands its reputation to a fresh key, it must burn an inheritance fee that doubles with each hop and multiplies with every branch sprouting from the same root — like a jetty whose next pile costs more as the line fans out. A sybil farm spawning thousands of children from one funded wallet gets no cheap avatars; the fan-out fee grows geometrically until splitting costs more than courting real counterparties, and the nadir of clone economies, mass identity at zero marginal cost, is priced out of existence.
